title: Automation complexity and overlap review
objective: Reduce operational complexity only after evidence shows which workflows are redundant, superseded or over-scheduled. Build an inventory and consolidation plan without changing schedules or deleting workflows in the analysis phase.

audit_observation.risk: The system is large enough that stale contracts, duplicate ownership, pointer drift and overlapping writer behavior can become primary failure modes.

required_work: Inventory every current workflow on fresh main with trigger, schedule, permissions, concurrency group, writer paths, owner, downstream consumers and recent health state.
Identify duplicate or overlapping owner responsibilities and duplicated scheduled collection/research functions.
Identify writer workflows that share or bypass the canonical main-writer concurrency boundary.
Map stale, never-run, terminalized and superseded workflow families without assuming that old age alone means obsolete.
Identify workflow/action dependency maintenance issues, including Node runtime deprecation exposure, but separate warnings from actual failures.
Produce consolidation waves ordered by risk reduction and reversibility.
Recommend Codex changes only for high-confidence, bounded candidates with explicit rollback and post-change observation gates.
guardrails: Analysis phase performs no workflow deletion, schedule removal, permission expansion or branch deletion.
Do not merge workflows merely because names look similar.
Do not change market, research, portfolio or canonical semantics.
A terminalized historical workflow may be classified for lifecycle reconciliation, not silently deleted.
Every ARCHIVE or SCHEDULE_REMOVE recommendation requires a current replacement/evidence trail and rollback plan.
codex_handoff_condition: A workflow or cluster has high-confidence redundancy/supersession, bounded change scope, no semantic change, explicit tests and a reversible migration/rollback plan.
clean_noop_condition: No high-confidence redundancy or unsafe overlap is found and current workflow scale is justified by distinct owners and lifecycle contracts.
